summary: The change passes. It fixes the cause where it starts. Plan demonstrations had no field for the test seam, so a plan never had to name one. The change adds a `seam` field to `DemonstrationOutput` and to the stored `Demonstration`. In the stored record the field defaults to none, so old plan records still load. It also adds a rule to `admission::plan_findings`: a major finding, naming the criterion, when a behavior criterion's seam is missing or blank. The planner then has to revise the plan before the critic ever sees it, and the critic, producer and verifier briefs print the seam as `Test seam:`. I ran the new tests and all pass: the athena-core seam tests (two unit tests and two end-to-end planning tests), the athena-data record round-trip test, the athena-context rendering test, and the full athena-cli suite. Without the change these tests would fail, either to compile (no `seam` field) or on their assertions (no new finding). Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. The CHANGELOG entry names the root cause and cites the three jobs. The one finding is scope: five changed files are not on the expected-deliverables list. The plan listed all five, and they are needed (the check itself and test fixtures), so it is minor.
